summary: Both auth-mode identifier strings for this CLI -- internal/mcp/tools.go's context tool ("auth":{"type":...}) and internal/cli/agent_context.go's buildAgentContext (authMode, feeding the peloton-pp-cli agent-context command's own auth.mode field) -- must say "session_login", never any OAuth-flavored term ("oauth2_refresh" or similar). Peloton has no OAuth flow at all: POST /auth/login once with PELOTON_OAUTH_USERNAME/PASSWORD, then persist the resulting session. Any future regen or edit to either auth-mode string must preserve this and keep both files' values identical, since they describe the same underlying auth mechanism through two different front doors (MCP context tool vs. CLI agent-context command).
reason: MINOR #4b from a second live post-fix verification sweep: an earlier pass (mcp-context-tool-accurate-content.json) fixed the env_var descriptions in tools.go's context tool but missed the literal "type": "oauth2_refresh" value itself, and never checked agent_context.go's own authMode, which had the identical residual. Any OAuth-flavored wording here specifically caused a documented multi-hour dead-end debugging a nonexistent external OAuth provisioning service earlier in this project's history (see peloton-managed-oauth.json / doctor-persisted-credential-detection.json).
validated_outcome: go build/vet/test/govulncheck and verify_skill.py all green. New test TestAgentContextAuthModeAvoidsOAuthWording asserts agent-context's Auth.Mode == "session_login"; TestHandleContextDescribesPelotonNotCRM extended to assert the MCP context tool's JSON never contains the substring "oauth2_refresh".
